{"subject": "Flow Step Output", "description": "TypeScript implementation spec for the Exaix request/plan API: types, error hierarchy, and handler logic", "steps": [{"step": 1, "title": "Core domain types", "description": "```typescript
type RequestStatus =
  | "queued"
  | "planning"
  | "running"
  | "cancelling"
  | "succeeded"
  | "failed"
  | "cancelled";

const TERMINAL_STATUSES = new Set<RequestStatus>(["succeeded", "failed", "cancelled"]);

interface RequestProgress {
  percent: number;
  currentStep: string | null;
  totalSteps: number;
}

interface ExaixRequest {
  id: string;
  tenantId: string;
  status: RequestStatus;
  input: Record<string, unknown>;
  result: Record<string, unknown> | null;
  error: { code: string; message: string } | null;
  planId: string | null;
  progress: RequestProgress | null;
  createdAt: string;
  updatedAt: string;
}

type PlanStepStatus = "pending" | "running" | "succeeded" | "failed" | "skipped";

interface PlanStep {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  status: PlanStepStatus;
  startedAt: string | null;
  finishedAt: string | null;
}

interface Plan {
  id: string;
  version: number;
  requestId: string;
  steps: PlanStep[];
  createdAt: string;
}

const VALID_TRANSITIONS: Record<RequestStatus, readonly RequestStatus[]> = {
  queued: ["planning", "cancelled"],
  planning: ["running", "failed"],
  running: ["succeeded", "failed", "cancelling"],
  cancelling: ["cancelled", "succeeded"],
  succeeded: [],
  failed: [],
  cancelled: [],
};

function isValidTransition(from: RequestStatus, to: RequestStatus): boolean {
  return VALID_TRANSITIONS[from].includes(to);
}
```"}, {"step": 2, "title": "Error hierarchy matching the retryable contract", "description": "```typescript
interface ErrorBody {
  error: { code: string; message: string; retryable: boolean };
}

abstract class ApiError extends Error {
  abstract readonly statusCode: number;
  abstract readonly retryable: boolean;
  constructor(readonly code: string, message: string) {
    super(message);
    this.name = this.constructor.name;
  }
  toBody(): ErrorBody {
    return { error: { code: this.code, message: this.message, retryable: this.retryable } };
  }
}

class ValidationError extends ApiError {
  readonly statusCode = 400;
  readonly retryable = false;
  constructor(message: string) { super("VALIDATION_ERROR", message); }
}

class UnauthenticatedError extends ApiError {
  readonly statusCode = 401;
  readonly retryable = false;
  constructor() { super("UNAUTHENTICATED", "Authentication required"); }
}

class NotFoundError extends ApiError {
  readonly statusCode = 404;
  readonly retryable = false;
  constructor() { super("NOT_FOUND", "Resource not found"); }
}

class ConflictError extends ApiError {
  readonly statusCode = 409;
  readonly retryable = false;
  constructor(message: string) { super("CONFLICT", message); }
}

class RateLimitedError extends ApiError {
  readonly statusCode = 429;
  readonly retryable = true;
  constructor(readonly retryAfterSeconds: number) { super("RATE_LIMITED", "Too many requests"); }
}

class InternalError extends ApiError {
  readonly statusCode = 500;
  readonly retryable = true;
  constructor() { super("INTERNAL_ERROR", "Operation failed"); } // generic — never leak cause
}
```
Note: `NotFoundError` is deliberately used both for missing IDs and cross-tenant access (per the architect's A01 fix) — the handler never distinguishes the two cases in its response, only in its internal audit log."}, {"step": 3, "title": "Atomic cancel/complete handler (CAS pattern)", "description": "```typescript
// Guards the running -> cancelling -> {cancelled|succeeded} race the architect flagged.
// Both writers use a conditional UPDATE; the loser's write affects 0 rows and is dropped, not retried.

interface StatusStore {
  casUpdateStatus(
    id: string,
    tenantId: string,
    from: readonly RequestStatus[],
    to: RequestStatus,
  ): Promise<boolean>; // true if the row was updated, false if `from` no longer matched
}

async function markSucceeded(store: StatusStore, id: string, tenantId: string): Promise<void> {
  const updated = await store.casUpdateStatus(id, tenantId, ["running", "cancelling"], "succeeded");
  if (!updated) {
    // Another writer already moved this request to a terminal state first — expected under the race, not an error.
    return;
  }
}

async function markCancelled(store: StatusStore, id: string, tenantId: string): Promise<void> {
  await store.casUpdateStatus(id, tenantId, ["cancelling"], "cancelled");
  // No-op if the completion writer already won; per architect step 3, completion wins silently.
}

async function requestCancel(store: StatusStore, id: string, tenantId: string, current: ExaixRequest): Promise<{ status: RequestStatus }> {
  if (TERMINAL_STATUSES.has(current.status)) {
    throw new ConflictError(`Request ${id} is already in a terminal state`);
  }
  if (current.status === "cancelling") {
    return { status: "cancelling" }; // idempotent no-op, per architect step 3
  }
  const target: RequestStatus = current.status === "queued" ? "cancelled" : "cancelling";
  const updated = await store.casUpdateStatus(id, tenantId, [current.status], target);
  if (!updated) throw new ConflictError(`Request ${id} state changed concurrently`);
  return { status: target };
}
```"}, {"step": 4, "title": "SSE resume handler skeleton", "description": "```typescript
interface SseEvent {
  seq: number;
  event: "status" | "progress" | "step" | "resync";
  data: ExaixRequest;
}

interface EventBuffer {
  since(requestId: string, lastSeq: number | null): SseEvent[] | "gap"; // "gap" = buffer rolled past lastSeq
}

async function streamEvents(
  req: { headers: { get(name: string): string | null } },
  requestId: string,
  tenantId: string,
  buffer: EventBuffer,
  fetchCurrent: (id: string, tenantId: string) => Promise<ExaixRequest>,
  write: (event: SseEvent) => void,
): Promise<void> {
  const lastEventIdHeader = req.headers.get("Last-Event-ID");
  const lastSeq = lastEventIdHeader ? Number(lastEventIdHeader) : null;

  if (lastSeq !== null) {
    const backlog = buffer.since(requestId, lastSeq);
    if (backlog === "gap") {
      const current = await fetchCurrent(requestId, tenantId);
      write({ seq: lastSeq, event: "resync", data: current }); // full snapshot, client resets
    } else {
      for (const evt of backlog) write(evt);
    }
  }
  // Live subscription continues from here in the actual transport layer.
}
```
This close-outs the architect's four review points into buildable code: `VALID_TRANSITIONS` enforces the state machine centrally rather than scattered `if` checks, `casUpdateStatus` gives the completion-wins-over-cancel race a single atomic implementation point, `ApiError` subclasses guarantee every response matches the `{code, message, retryable}` contract, and `streamEvents` implements `Last-Event-ID` resume with an explicit `resync` fallback when the buffer has rolled over."}]}
